plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A dramatic, bowl-shaped flower head up to 30 cm across. Its crown of silky pink bracts surrounds a center of soft, fuzzy florets. It looks part artichoke and part sunburst, and it stands out against the leathery green foliage of the shrub.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mainly winter through spring (June to October), so it is in bloom on October 1
plants.location: Fynbos of the Western and Eastern Cape, South Africa
plants.funFact: The king protea is South Africa's national flower. It belongs to a very old plant family that dates back to the supercontinent Gondwana, and it has evolved to survive the periodic wildfires of its fynbos home.

plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: Goblet-shaped lilac-pink blooms rise from the bare ground with no leaves. They look like crocuses but are larger, and they light up damp meadows just as autumn begins.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to autumn (August to October), so it is in bloom on October 1
plants.location: Meadows and woodland edges across Europe, including Britain and Central Europe
plants.funFact: Autumn crocus is often called 'naked ladies' because the flowers appear without leaves. The foliage emerges the following spring. The plant is highly toxic, but it is also the source of colchicine, a compound used in medicine and in plant breeding.

plants.name: Cosmos bipinnatus
plants.description: Airy, daisy-like flowers float on slender stems above feathery, finely cut foliage. They sway in the breeze and attract bees and butterflies late into the season.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early summer until the first frost, so it is still blooming on October 1 in mild-autumn regions
plants.location: Native to Mexico and the southern United States; widely grown in gardens across the Northern Hemisphere
plants.funFact: The name 'cosmos' comes from a Greek word meaning 'order' or 'harmony,' a reference to the neat symmetry of the petals. The plants flower best in lean soil, and rich soil gives you leaves instead of blooms.

plants.name: Symphyotrichum novae-angliae
plants.description: A tall, bushy wildflower that becomes a mass of violet-purple daisies with bright golden centers. It is a bright spot in autumn fields, roadsides and prairies.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer through autumn (August to October), so it is in bloom on October 1
plants.location: Meadows, prairies and roadsides of eastern and central North America
plants.funFact: Late-season blooms make this aster a key fuel stop for migrating monarch butterflies. They stock up on its nectar before their long journey south to Mexico.
